channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: NFP or Iran: Which factor will break the US Dollar Index out of its consolidation?
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY) trades around 99.95 at the time of writing on Friday, virtually unchanged on the day, as investors refrain from placing aggressive bets ahead of the release of the July US employment report.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver rises, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) rose on Friday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $64.34 per troy ounce, up 4.58% from the $61.52 it cost on Thursday.

item.title: US Dollar: Labour market still solid – Danske Bank
item.description: Danske Research Team expects United States (US) Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) to rise by 70k in July, with the unemployment rate steady at 4.2% and average hourly earnings up 0.3% m/m.

item.title: Swiss Franc: Funding currency weakness extends – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong note the Swiss Franc (CHF) remains under pressure as carry trade funding demand grows and recent Japanese Yen (JPY) intervention reinforces CHF’s role as a preferred funding currency.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Upside risk tied to 0.7075 break against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note AUD/USD has pulled back to 0.7032 after failing to clear 0.7075, with intraday price action expected to remain range-bound between 0.7015 and 0.7055.

item.title: Japanese Yen holds onto weekly losses amid absence of US-Japan intervention follow-up
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) has underperformed its major currency peers this week due to a lack of follow-up joint intervention by the United States (US) and Japan.

item.title: NZD/USD Price Forecast: Consolidates above 0.5860/weekly low as bulls look to US NFP
item.description: The NZD/USD pair seesaws between tepid gains and minor losses through the first half of the European session on Friday as traders opt to move to the sidelines ahead of the release of the crucial US Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) report.

item.title: Indian Rupee drops as oil price rebounds, US NFP awaited
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) falls slightly against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday in the countdown to the United States (US) Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) data for July at 06:00 PM IST or 12:30 GMT.

item.title: Oil: Volatile range trading outlook – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s Joe DeLaura details how renewed United States (US)–Iran tensions and disruptions at the Strait of Hormuz have driven a sharp rally and subsequent correction in Brent and West Texas Intermediate (WTI).

item.title: US Nonfarm Payrolls expected to rise by 80K in July
item.description: The United States (US) Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) is set to release the Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) data for July on Friday at 12:30 GMT.

item.title: British Pound eases below 1.3450 as markets brace for the US Nonfarm Payrolls report
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) nurses minor gains against the (USD) for the second consecutive day on Friday, with the GBP/USD retreating to levels just below 1.3450 at the time of writing.

item.title: Czech Koruna: CZK softens against Euro as CNB waits – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Tatha Ghose reports that the Czech National Bank (CNB) kept its policy rate at 3.75% and returned to a wait-and-see stance after June’s 25bp hike, despite still citing upside inflation risks.

item.title: Gold looks to build on momentum beyond $4,300 as traders await US NFP amid Fed hike bets
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) touches a fresh daily high during the first half of the European session on Friday, with bulls making a fresh attempt to build on the momentum further beyond the $4,300 mark.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Higher US rate volatility favors safe havens – BNY
item.description: BNY's David Tam argues that rising U.S. rate volatility should favor safe-haven currencies, with the Yen historically benefiting from such episodes. Heavy speculative JPY shorts add another catalyst, as appreciation could force position unwinds and trigger a sharper squeeze.

item.title: Euro remains stronger against Canadian Dollar as German Industrial output beats forecasts
item.description: EUR/CAD gains ground after two days of losses, trading around 1.6160 during the European hours on Friday. The currency cross maintains its strength as the Euro (EUR) holds its ground following the latest data release from Destatis.

item.title: Equities: Stocks pressured by higher yields and energy risks - Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank strategists notes that the S&P 500 slipped as geopolitical developments and higher yields pressured sentiment. Energy outperformed while industrials and materials lagged.

item.title: Japanese Yen trades broadly flat against US Dollar, NFP data eyed
item.description: The Japanese Yen (JPY) trades almost flat against the US Dollar (USD) at around 158.42 during the European trading session on Friday. The USD/JPY pair consolidates as investors await the United States (US) Nonfarm Payrolls (NFP) data for July, which will be published at 12:30 GMT.

item.title: British Pound holds steady around 213.00 as fiscal concerns and rate gap undermine Yen
item.description: The GBP/JPY cross struggles to extend its positive move witnessed over the past three days and consolidates around the 213.00 mark, or the top end of its weekly range, through the early European session on Friday.

item.title: Silver Price Forecasts: XAG/USD bulls are eroding resistance at the $63.30 area
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) resumes its near-term bullish trend on Friday, after a brief hesitation on Thursday, reaching fresh six-week highs at $63.90, although it is still due to confirm the break of the resistance area at $63.30.

item.title: Copper: Near record highs on tight supply – ING
item.description: ING’s Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey report Copper trading comfortably above $14,000/t, close to record highs, supported by tariff-related stockpiling into the US and tight physical markets elsewhere. They flag low inventories, constrained mine supply and ongoing disruptions as key supports.

item.title: Forex Today: Markets turn attention from Middle East to Nonfarm Payrolls
item.description: Here is what you need to know on Friday, August 7:

item.title: Dow Jones futures move little ahead of US Nonfarm Payrolls
item.description: Dow Jones futures inch lower 0.04% to trade around 53,990 during European hours on Friday. Meanwhile, S&P 500 futures gain 0.07% to trade near 7,740 and Nasdaq 100 futures gain 0.29%, trading near 29,570.

item.title: British Pound: Upside fades below 1.3410 against US Dollar - UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann highlight that GBP/USD has been confined to tight ranges around 1.3455, with a slight increase in near-term downside momentum. They expect any intraday decline to stay within 1.3430–1.3475.

item.title: Euro: US payrolls could cap gains against the US Dollar - Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Michael Pfister notes that reduced expectations for Federal Reserve (Fed) tightening have helped EUR/USD climb, but questions how justified this move is.

item.title: USD/CAD Price Forecast: Bullish Flag pattern underway
item.description: The Canadian Dollar (CAD) trades marginally lower against the US Dollar (USD) on Friday, with the USD/CAD pair edging up to near 1.4023 in the European trading session.

item.title: Euro steadies against the British Pound following another rejection at the 0.8580 area
item.description: The Euro (EUR) trades practically flat against the British Pound (GBP) on Friday, moving in a tight range above 0.8560 during the early European session, following another rejection at the 0.8680 area.

item.title: AUD/USD Price Forecast: Flat lines below mid-0.7000s/100-SMA as bulls await US NFP
item.description: The AUD/USD pair finds some support near the 38.2% Fibonacci retracement level of the May-June corrective slide and, for now, seems to have stalled its pullback from the highest level since June 17, around 0.7065, touched earlier this week.

item.title: EUR/JPY Price Forecast: Holds losses near 182.50 as bearish bias prevails
item.description: EUR/JPY halts its three-day winning streak, trading around 182.50 during the early European hours on Friday. The currency cross is retaining a bearish near-term bias as spot holds below both the nine-period and 50-period Exponential Moving Averages (EMAs).

item.title: Gold: Breakout holds as US payrolls loom – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong note Gold has retained most recent gains after breaking key resistance, supported by lower Oil, softer yields, central bank and ETF buying and technical factors.

item.title: Equities: Sector rotation dominates risk-off – Danske Bank
item.description: Danske Research Team reports equities closed lower in a 2026-style risk-off session driven by sentiment rather than macro or earnings. Higher Oil prices weighed, but the key feature was pronounced rotation from cyclicals into defensives such as energy, consumer staples and health care.
